summary: The user's decision closed both Phase 7 blockers as option 1: both axioms landed as-is. Neither axiom was dropped or weakened, no max_time was raised on any bimodal example, no expected verdict was adjusted, and no example definition was edited; the cost regression stays recorded with its mechanism explicitly unestablished. The substantive new work -- making bimodal non-gating -- did not need a new mechanism: a `development` marker was already registered, already carried by all six release-gating `-m` expressions, already enforced by test_unstable_deselection_wiring.py, and already documented as TESTING_GUIDE 8.14, whose own text said no test claimed it. Applying it is what took bimodal off the gate. All 313 bimodal tests now carry it via a path-scoped pytest_collection_modifyitems hook in bimodal/tests/conftest.py; both gating expressions collect 0 of 313, and `-m development` collects all 313. TDD followed: the contract test was written first and confirmed RED (3 failed/4 passed) before the hook existed, and it caught a real leak -- the first hook had no path check, and because pytest hands such a hook the ENTIRE session's item list, it marked all 2534 tests in the repo and the gating expression collected zero. That leak is invisible to per-root checks and only appears in the mixed-root `pytest tests src/model_checker` collection CI actually runs. Running the broader suites (which the previous dispatch recorded as not run) surfaced 3 genuine failures OUTSIDE the bimodal tree, caused by this task's own axioms: tests/cli/conftest.py's tiny CLI example used bimodal with no explicit max_time, and the axioms take that example from ~0.42s decided to ~4.2-4.7s, so it now always times out at the inherited 1s budget, finds no model, and leaves -p/-z/-i with nothing extra to print. Fixed by switching that fixture to logos (~0.001s), matching the precedent already documented in the same file -- not absorbed into the bimodal exclusion. Final: pytest tests/ 601 passed/5 skipped/0 failed; gating parallel pass 2088 passed/1 skipped/0 failed exit 0; gating serial pass 9 passed/2527 deselected exit 0; tests/ci 92 passed; tests/cli 90 passed/1 skipped. Bimodal itself unchanged at 308 passed/5 failed -- accepted and non-gating.

decisions_made: Applied the development marker as a THEORY-WIDE blanket, which TESTING_GUIDE 8.14 otherwise forbids ('per-test, not per-module or per-theory'). The user's declaration is about the whole theory, not a list of incomplete behaviours, so a per-test set-membership marking would misrepresent it and need editing on every commit adding a bimodal test. 8.14 was amended to record this as the one authorized exception, with the accepted risk stated (a bimodal test regressing from passing to failing no longer gates) and three bounds on it.

Deliberately did NOT add `-m "not development"` to code/pyproject.toml's addopts. That would be a second exclusion mechanism parallel to the repo's established one (marker + gating-driver -m, enforced by test_unstable_deselection_wiring.py), and it would make `pytest <bimodal path>` and `./run_tests.py bimodal` collect zero tests and report success -- the silent-green failure mode 8.14 exists to prevent. CONSEQUENCE STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a bare local `pytest` from code/ still collects and can still fail on bimodal. The team lead's requirement was phrased as 'the default/release test run'; the release and gating runs are structurally covered, the bare local run is not. If the bare local run was meant too, that is a one-line addopts change plus an ergonomics fix in run_tests.py and needs a deliberate decision.

Fixed the three tests/cli/test_flag_matrix.py failures at their root (the fixture's theory choice) rather than by raising a max_time or by extending the bimodal exclusion. Switching to logos matches the precedent and rationale _CVC5_COMPATIBLE_EXAMPLE already documents in the same file, and removes a gating CLI test's dependence on the deliberately-non-gating theory's solver cost.

Did NOT strengthen test_output_affecting_boolean_flag_changes_output to ignore the volatile Solver Run Time line, despite having direct evidence it currently passes vacuously for the print_constraints parameter. ModelStructure.print_constraints() has zero callers, so -p is a genuinely unwired flag; strengthening the assertion without wiring the flag would turn a currently-green gating suite red on a defect unrelated to this task. Flagged as a follow-up covering both halves.

Recorded, rather than silently accepted, that the development marker's owning task holds a Phase 6 exit criterion ('pytest --collect-only -m development -q collects zero tests') that this dispatch makes false by design. TESTING_GUIDE 8.14's 'Currently marked' paragraph, the one place that statement lived, was updated.
